public_rationale: This claim reports two findings from a study. GovInfoSecurity (ISMG), on 2026-05-08, reported both. It said 94% of agents in the Elloe AI Lab-led study that keep memory across sessions were vulnerable to poisoning attacks (e1). It also said nearly 90% of all tested agents drifted measurably from their original goals after roughly 30 steps (e1). That matches Marcus's 94% figure and fits his 89.4% figure. Wallstreetcn, on 2026-05-06, gave the exact figures: 89.4% goal drift after about 30 steps and 94% of memory-augmented agents at risk of poisoning (e2). The paper itself was not found, so this assessment rests on news reports of its findings, which the contract accepts.
limitations: The primary paper was not found. The assessment rests on news reports.
The exact 89.4% figure appears only in the Wallstreetcn report, which may draw on Marcus's post. ISMG gives 'nearly 90%'.
Wallstreetcn also reports 67% goal drift after 15 steps. The paper may define or measure drift in more than one way.
The study's methods and its definitions of drift and vulnerability were not checked.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: In the new study, 89.4% of agents drifted from goals after about 30 steps, and 94% of memory-augmented agents were vulnerable to poisoning.

our_interpretation: This claim reports the study's findings. It holds if the study reported about 89.4% (nearly 90%) of agents drifting from goals after roughly 30 steps, and 94% of memory-augmented agents vulnerable to poisoning.
A reputable news report of the paper's findings counts as evidence when the paper is unavailable.
criteria.support_condition: The study, or a reliable report of it, gives roughly 89.4% goal drift after about 30 steps and 94% poisoning vulnerability among memory-augmented agents.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The study, or a reliable report of it, gives materially different figures for either statistic, or does not report them.
